title: 3D Lab · Stellar Odyssey
scene: Monochrome black hole with bent light and a camera approaching the accretion disk
frozen: Automatic motion is reduced according to your system preference.
running: Scroll to weave through the stars and fly just above the accretion disk.

start.description: The camera starts close to the black hole amid {{count}} stars. Scroll down to observe bent light from changing viewpoints.

travel.description: The camera weaves left–right–left–right–left. Stars grow very slightly on approach; hot gas lanes rotate faster near the center.

end.description: Foreground light crosses the shadow while the rear disk bends into two arcs. The camera stops just above the emitting disk, with the black hole on the right.

story.running: Scrub Portal / Works / Finale. Seed and Works origin persist through holds and reversals. Production typography is not integrated.
story.end: Contact rest point. Seed {{seed}}, default phase {{phase}} without a Works visit. This space provides the final chapter’s full scroll range.

notes.hero: The last O is a real DOM anchor for R2.2. The current scene only checks camera poses; this is not the redesigned Hero.
notes.portal: 1.75 viewports: approach O → expanding core / blackout → ejection. One shared HDR image; observer stays outside the horizon.
notes.about: Parked camera, black hole to the right with a reading area to the left.

notes.education: 1.75 viewports; reframe during the first 25%, then park for the star map. The map is not integrated.
notes.experience: Keep the black hole in the background while reading. The main page uses the DOM-guided meteor.
notes.departure: Camera handoff from Experience to Works; the DOM-guided meteor is integrated on the main page.
notes.works: Three R0.2 figures: Centaurus / Gemini / Cygnus. Slow orbit with preserved orientation and stable selection controls.
notes.finale: 2.25 viewports: retract labels → orbit / curved trails → 10% compression → collision / nebula → gas infall / black hole. Every layer uses the same progress; stop or reverse at any point.
